messages:
lee: alert from uptime-monitor -> multiple customer 504s and elevated p99 latency on hosted inference for tenant 'polar-read'. seeing a flood of queued requests and queue-depth metrics pegged.
nora: details? request ids or sample traces?
lee: pasted a snippet from gateway logs + batcher counters:
```
2026-03-16T14:08:12Z gateway: tenant=polar-read req=QID-9a1b status=504 reason=queue_timeout queue_depth=1123 max_queue=1200
2026-03-16T14:08:13Z batcher: continuous_backlog=78 inflight_batches=24 kv_cache_misses=12
2026-03-16T14:08:14Z runtime: p95=4200ms p99=9800ms tokens/sec=50
```
support-jen: customer is on a high-qps test harness right now, says hits spiked ~3x for last 20m. they're seeing consistent 504s.
maya: spike + continuous batcher backlog = classic saturation. any autoscaler events? I see no recent scale-up for that pool in logs.
sre-bot: autoscaler: no scaling events for pool 'hosted-eu-small' in last 30m. current utilization 96%.
lee: repro steps from support: run burst script at ~350 rps with seq len ~512 and concurrency 200. reproduces 504s within ~2m.
eng-oncall: tagging in. first priority: mitigate customer impact. quick suggestions: 1) route tenant to secondary pool, 2) temporarily increase gateway queue_depth limit, 3) throttle customer at ingress.
nora: routing is non-trivial right now, pools are full. we can add an emergency route to dedicated fallback but need prod-config change and risk cross-tenant perf noise.
maya: quick fix: enable ingress soft-throttle (drop new requests over threshold) for that tenant to stop queue pileup. will also reduce p99.
lee: trying soft-throttle now: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/tenants/polar-read/actions -d '{"throttle":"soft","rate":80}'`
lee: controlplane responded 202 accepted.
support-jen: customer reports a few hundred fewer 504s immediately, still some tail events but much reduced :thumbsup:
eng-oncall: good. next: need root cause. backlog suggests continuous-batcher can't flush due to long-running model tokens/sec drop. check model hotpath metrics and cold kv-cache churn.
maya: kv-cache miss rate jumped during spike; batcher latency per-batch went up from 120ms to 1100ms. suspect GPU preemption or noisy neighbor on that host set.
lee: host-level logs show occasional GPU scheduler preemption events at ~14:06:xx.
```
[14:06:21] nv-sched: preempt evict kernel_id=0x4f3a reason=maintenance
[14:06:23] nv-sched: preempt resume kernel_id=0x4f3a
```
nora: if preemption is true, runtime drops throughput and batcher backlog grows. mitigation: pin critical pools to no-preempt hardware or migrate tenant off those nodes.
eng-oncall: action items:
- (lee) keep soft-throttle in place and monitor p99 (10m)
- (maya) check pool allocation & schedule a migration if preempt events persist
- (nora) craft rollback plan if routing change causes regressions
- (support-jen) notify customer of mitigation and ETA
I'll also open a post-incident ticket to investigate autoscaler thresholds and queue_depth defaults.
lee: p99 down to ~700ms after throttle, customer confirms improved UX.
support-jen: customer is satisfied for now but wants a follow-up on why autoscaler didn't trigger.
maya: noted. I'll attach batcher traces and node-level telemetry to the incident ticket (INC-2026-045).
eng-oncall: thanks team. leaving this thread open until migration or config changes complete. will post updates here.
